groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material:
White meat, such as chicken, may raise blood cholesterol levels as much as red meat does. This finding surprised researchers, who admitted they didn't expect that eating white meat would lead to higher blood cholesterol levels.
In the study, researchers looked at 113 healthy people. The participants ate three different diets. These were a red meat diet which is primarily beef, a white meat diet which is mostly chicken and turkey, and a vegetarian protein diet. Each diet period was four weeks. Between the diet periods, participants had a break, during which they ate their regular foods. In addition, participants had blood tests at the start and finish of each new diet.
The results showed that white and red meat diets had the same effects on blood cholesterol levels. Further, both diets increased blood cholesterol levels compared with the diet built on vegetarian protein sources.
The team acknowledged that it is possible that white meat is better for our health than red meat despite their findings. This is because other effects of red meat consumption could contribute to heart disease independent of cholesterol. Their main recommendations are that people eat less of both kinds of meat and more vegetarian protein.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material:
At around half past nine this morning, a trailer attached to a lorry turned over at the crossing of High Street in Milton. Hundreds of frozen turkeys were spilled all over the road. It is reported that nobody was hurt in the incident, but police said it may affect traffic and Christmas dinners. With just one week to go before Christmas, there are worries that local supermarket supplies of this holiday favorite may be affected.
A police spokeswoman said that officers were currently in attendance at the scene. She stated that the driver of the lorry had been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving.
The crossing on High Street is a well-known accident blackspot. This year alone, there have been seven traffic accidents at this location. Thankfully, none of these accidents have resulted in serious injury.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material:
India launched its helicopter taxi service on Monday, promising to ferry customers the 40 miles between Bangalore's Electronic City tech hub and the International Airport terminal in 15 minutes.
Customers can book their helicopter ride through a mobile app. The service, which claims to be the first of its kind in India, offers only one route, but Bangalore airport will add more once it gets approval.
Helicopter taxi is not an affordable option for many travelers. A car ride for the same journey costs less than half as much. But Bangalore airport says it is a competitive alternative to a car ride for tech executives in a hurry. "A large number of high-class travelers, including CEOs, have to spend more than three hours by road to get there and that is a loss of time," a Bangalore airport spokesperson said. "This is not a low cost option, but it is an option," she added.
The helicopters ferried around eight customers to the airport on their first day. The company that owns and operates the service is called Thumby Aviation. It previously specialized in private charter flights for government officials.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
W: Hi, I wish to buy some cheese for a barbecue this weekend.
M: What kind would you like?
W: Sorry, I don't know much about cheese. What type do you think would be suitable for a barbecue?
M: That's easy! For a barbecue, you could have any cheese you want. I imagine there will be different foods and people will just help themselves and eat at their own pace, right?
W: Yes, exactly. It will be very casual. We will just be a small group of friends gathering together at Washington Park. There will be around 20 of us, including children.
M: Great! So you could have different types of cheese. How much would you like to spend?
W: Not very much. Let's say $30.
M: I would suggest having at least one soft cheese and one hard cheese. That will offer you a good variety to suit different people's tastes.
W: That sounds good. What's the difference between a soft cheese and a hard cheese?
M: Well, it depends. But generally speaking, soft cheeses are creamy and go well with sweet things like honey and jam. I would suggest something like this Spanish goat cheese. It's only $15, a very good price. You can spread it on bread with a knife, and then add a tiny bit of honey on top. It's delicious. Children love it.
W: Okay, great. What about a hard cheese?
M: Yes, for hard cheese, I would recommend this Italian one here. It has a very strong smell and a dry flavor. You can cut it into thin slices and eat it on its own. It's $16.
W: Okay, I'll take both. Thank you for your help.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
M: Our school is replacing printed textbooks with e-textbooks next semester. I can't wait.
W: Really? What about the cost, not only buying all those tablets, but the software and electronic infrastructure that goes with it, not to mention retraining all the teachers and administration staff?
M: Sure, the initial expenditure will be high, but much lower afterwards. Besides that, tablet prices continue to drop and are becoming increasingly affordable. Anyway, tablets help students learn up to 80% faster.
W: Not necessarily. Tablets have too many distractions. Students may pay attention to apps, games and websites instead of their teachers. In fact, research suggests that people who read printed text comprehend more, remember more and learn 30% more than those who read digital text.
M: Yes. But tablets contain many technological features that are not found in printed textbooks. Think about it. Students are able to highlight and edit text, write notes and search for information much more quickly than they can with printed textbooks. And what about all those trees that are cut down to make printed books?
W: Actually, manufacturing tablets is environmentally destructive and dangerous to human health. The health impacts from making one electronic reader are 70 times greater than those from making a single printed book. A lot of minerals are extracted from the earth to make electronic readers. It does far more damage to the environment.
M: Yes. But the software for electronic readers can be updated instantly without the need for buying a whole lot of new books. That's better for the environment.
W: But the core curriculum doesn't change that much. Printed textbooks that are not brand new, still contain the basic relevant information of core subjects.
M: Well, I'm looking forward to the change.
W: I'll stick with my printed books.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
In social psychology, the term "person perception" refers to the mental processes that we use to form impressions of other people. It includes not just how we form these impressions, but the conclusions we make about other people based on our impressions. Consider how often you make this kind of judgment every day. When you meet with a new coworker, you immediately begin to develop an initial impression of this person. When you visit the grocery store, you might draw conclusions about the cashier who checks you out.
Obviously, person perception is a very subjective process that can be affected by a number of variables, including the characteristics of the person you are observing, the context of the situation, your own personal traits, and your past experiences.
One of the techniques we use in person perception is social categorization. In this process, we mentally categorize people into different groups based on common characteristics.
Problems with this technique include the fact that it can lead to errors and prejudice. Imagine that you are getting on a bus. There are only two seats available. One is next to a small, elderly woman; the other is next to a muscular, fierce-looking man. You sit next to the elderly woman, who unfortunately turns out to be quite skilled at picking pockets.
Because of social categorization, you immediately judge the woman as harmless, and the man as threatening, leading to the loss of your wallet.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Despite smartphones and social media, young people today are as socially competent as those from the previous generation. At least this is what a new study suggests.
For the study, researchers compared teacher and parent evaluations of American children who started kindergarten in 1998, with those who began school in 2010. The former group entered kindergarten when mobile phones were luxuries. The latter group started school when mobile devices were widespread.
Results showed both groups of children were rated similarly on important social skills. These included their ability to form and maintain friendships and get along with people who are different. They were also rated similarly on self-control, such as the ability to regulate their temper.
In virtually every comparison made, ratings of social skills either remain constant or improved for the children born later. There was one exception: Social skills were slightly lower for children who accessed online games and social networking sites many times a day.
Adults are worried when technological change starts to undermine traditional relationships, particularly the parent-child relationship.
The introduction of telephones, automobiles and radio all led to moral panic among adults of the time, because the technology allowed children to enjoy more freedom. Fears over screen-based technology represent the most recent panic in response to technological change. But overall, the study found little evidence that time spent on screens was hurting social skills for most children.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
It's easy to spend all day searching for inspiration. You can find incredible videos, articles and news stories about the success of others.
The problem is that consuming the success and ideas of others is passive inspiration. Every time you read an article or listen to an interview, you're practicing passive inspiration. You might learn something, but you don't actually have to do anything. Hearing about other people's success isn't the same as creating your own.
Instead, it is through the process of active inspiration—the act of creating things, applying new ideas to our goals, and making mistakes that we discover who we are and what is important to us. Furthermore, active inspiration is what results in long-term passion and enthusiasm. Watching someone else's success might leave you feeling excited for a few minutes. However, taking action and applying a new idea to your life will inspire you more than anything someone else can say.
Learning and listening can help you think about things in a different way. But creating, producing, and experimenting is what drives you forward. Passive inspiration can give you ideas, but active inspiration will give you power.
Too often we spend our lives consuming the world around us instead of creating it. And what matters is the power your actions have to inspire you. The best inspiration comes from the application of ideas, not the consumption of them.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the news report about the study?
options: It examines the effect of cholesterol on people's health.
Its participants all had high blood cholesterol levels.
It questions the benefits of a vegetarian protein diet.
Its finding came as a surprise to the researchers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the news report about the study? 

 【翻译】 从新闻报道中我们对这项研究了解到什么? 
 A)  它检验了胆固醇对人们健康的影响。 
 B)  它的参与者都有高血胆固醇水平。 
 C)  它质疑素食蛋白饮食的益处。 
 D)  它的发现让研究人员感到意外。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Its finding came as a surprise to the researchers. 
 【定位】 P1 This finding surprised researchers, who admitted they didn't expect that eating white meat would lead to higher blood cholesterol levels. 
 这一发现令研究者们感到意外,他们承认自己没有料到吃白肉会导致血液胆固醇水平升高。 

 【信号】 情绪信号词 surprised 。答案落点不是平铺的数据句,而是带情绪色彩的 This finding surprised researchers,再用 who admitted they didn't expect 加重——新闻里出现"意外/没料到"这种态度词,往往就是出题点。 

 【替换】 This finding surprised researchers ↔ Its finding came as a surprise to the researchers 动词 surprised 改写成名词 a surprise 
 who admitted they didn't expect ↔ came as a surprise "没料到"与"意外"同义互证 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借了原文反复出现的 blood cholesterol levels 里的 cholesterol 一词,把研究说成"考察胆固醇对健康的影响";但录音考察的是"不同肉类的饮食对胆固醇的影响",胆固醇是被测的结果而非被研究的起因,A 把对象说反了。  借用原文：blood cholesterol levels 

 B) 与原文相反 B 说参与者"都是高胆固醇",但第二段原文是 researchers looked at 113 healthy people(113 名健康人);B 盗用了 cholesterol levels 这个反复出现的词,再加个绝对的 all,把"健康人"悄悄换成"高胆固醇人群",与原文相反。  借用原文：researchers looked at 113 healthy people 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说研究"质疑素食蛋白饮食的好处",借的是原文真出现过的 a vegetarian protein diet;但原文第四段恰恰是 eat...more vegetarian protein(建议多吃素食蛋白),研究从头到尾力挺素食蛋白、绝无质疑,属无中生有又反向。  借用原文：a vegetarian protein diet

questions.prompt: What did the researchers acknowledge?
options: They do not know all the effects of eating meat.
Red meat itself does not cause heart diseases.
White meat may be healthier than red meat.
Vegetarian protein may be easier to absorb.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the researchers acknowledge? 

 【翻译】 研究人员承认了什么? 
 A)  他们不知道吃肉的所有影响。 
 B)  红肉本身不会导致心脏病。 
 C)  白肉可能比红肉更健康。 
 D)  素食蛋白可能更容易被吸收。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） White meat may be healthier than red meat. 
 【定位】 P4 The team acknowledged that it is possible that white meat is better for our health than red meat despite their findings. 
 研究团队承认,尽管有这些发现,白肉仍有可能比红肉更有益于我们的健康。 

 【信号】 题干同词 acknowledged 引出让步 。答案句正是题干 acknowledge 在原文里的对应词 The team acknowledged that it is possible that,其后 white meat is better for our health than red meat 就是承认的内容;"题干动词在原文复现"是最稳的定位信号。 

 【替换】 white meat is better for our health than red meat ↔ White meat may be healthier than red meat better for our health 改写成 healthier 
 it is possible that ↔ may be it is possible that 等于 may 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 A 借了第四段 other effects of red meat consumption 里的 effects,说研究者"承认还不了解吃肉的全部影响";但原文只说红肉"另有别的影响可能致病",并没说研究者"不知道全部影响",A 把局部说法夸大成笼统的"全不知",属过度推断。  借用原文：other effects of red meat consumption 

 B) 与原文相反 B 借了原文 contribute to heart disease 里的 heart disease,说"红肉本身不致心脏病";但原文恰说红肉的别的影响"可能促成心脏病",方向正相反,B 把原文的肯定关系反成了否定。  借用原文：contribute to heart disease 

 D) 未提及 D 借了原文反复出现的 vegetarian protein,却安上一个原文压根没提的角度 absorb(更易吸收);全文只说建议多吃素食蛋白、它对胆固醇影响更小,从未谈"吸收",属无中生有。  借用原文：vegetarian protein

questions.prompt: What does the news report say about the accident at the crossing of High Street in Milton?
options: It may have been due to the lorry driver's drunk driving.
It may affect the local supply of turkeys for Christmas.
It interrupted traffic for several hours running.
It was caused by a lorry running into a trailer.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the news report say about the accident at the crossing of High Street in Milton? 

 【翻译】 新闻报道关于Milton High Street路口事故说了什么? 
 A)  这可能是由于卡车司机酒后驾驶造成的。 
 B)  这可能影响当地圣诞节火鸡的供应。 
 C)  这使交通连续中断了几个小时。 
 D)  这是由一辆卡车撞上拖车引起的。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It may affect the local supply of turkeys for Christmas. 
 【定位】 P1 It is reported that nobody was hurt in the incident, but police said it may affect traffic and Christmas dinners. With just one week to go before Christmas, there are worries that local supermarket supplies of this holiday favorite may be affected. 
 据报道，事故中无人受伤，但警方表示这可能影响交通和圣诞晚餐。距圣诞节仅剩一周，人们担心当地超市这一节日抢手货的供应可能受影响。 

 【信号】 转折 but 后接真正落点 。答案藏在转折词后面：nobody was hurt in the incident, but police said it may affect traffic and Christmas dinners 里 but 之后才是报道强调的影响，紧接着 supplies of this holiday favorite may be affected 进一步点明"节日抢手货"（即火鸡）供应受影响，这正是答案句。 

 【替换】 supplies of this holiday favorite may be affected ↔ It may affect the local supply of turkeys for Christmas. this holiday favorite=turkeys 
 may be affected ↔ It may affect 被动转主动·affect 同词根 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音说司机 had been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving（涉嫌危险驾驶被捕），选项却写成 drunk driving（酒驾）。dangerous driving 与 drunk driving 长得像、都沾"driving"，但危险驾驶不等于酒驾，原文从没提到喝酒，属偷换。  借用原文：the driver of the lorry had been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 interrupted traffic for several hours running 里"中断交通"沾了原文 it may affect traffic 的边——traffic 确实被念到，所以听到就想选；但原文只说"可能影响交通"，从没说"中断了好几个小时"，several hours 是凭空加的时长。  借用原文：it may affect traffic and Christmas dinners 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 It was caused by a lorry running into a trailer 把 lorry、trailer 两个原词都用上了，极像答案；但原文是 a trailer attached to a lorry turned over——挂在卡车上的拖车翻倒，并不是"一辆卡车撞上一辆拖车"，选项把"翻车"歪曲成了"撞车"，动作对不上。  借用原文：a trailer attached to a lorry turned over at the crossing of High Street

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the crossing on High Street?
options: It has been the scene of several fatal accidents recently.
It is the spot that causes the local police a lot of worry.
It has witnessed several traffic accidents this year.
It is a location frequented by local traffic police.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the crossing on High Street? 

 【翻译】 关于High Street路口我们了解到什么? 
 A)  这里最近发生过几起致命事故。 
 B)  这是让当地警方十分担忧的地点。 
 C)  这里今年发生过几起交通事故。 
 D)  这是当地交警经常出现的地点。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It has witnessed several traffic accidents this year. 
 【定位】 P3 The crossing on High Street is a well-known accident blackspot. This year alone, there have been seven traffic accidents at this location. Thankfully, none of these accidents have resulted in serious injury. 
 高街的这个路口是出了名的事故黑点。仅今年一年，这个地点就发生了七起交通事故。所幸这些事故没有一起造成严重伤亡。 

 【信号】 数字+时间范围·具体数据句 。答案落在带具体数据的那句：This year alone, there have been seven traffic accidents at this location——"今年"这个时间范围加上"七起"这个数字，正是新闻里最常被设题的信息点，听到数字就该锁定。 

 【替换】 there have been seven traffic accidents ↔ It has witnessed several traffic accidents seven=several·具体数概括成"几起" 
 This year alone ↔ this year 时间范围一致·this year 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项 several fatal accidents 借用了原文 accident 一词，但 fatal（致命的，会死人）与原文恰好相反——录音明说 none of these accidents have resulted in serious injury（没有一起造成严重伤亡），更别提致命，方向反了。  借用原文：none of these accidents have resulted in serious injury 

 B) 未提及 选项 causes the local police a lot of worry 用了 police 这个原文出现过的词（A police spokeswoman、officers were currently in attendance）来诱选，但原文只说警方到场处理、发言人通报，从没说这个路口"让警方很担忧"，担忧是凭空加的。  借用原文：officers were currently in attendance at the scene 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 frequented by local traffic police 把 traffic（原文 it may affect traffic 念过）和 police（A police spokeswoman 念过）拼在一起，听着字字耳熟；但原文从没说"交警经常光顾这个路口"，frequented 这层意思是编出来的。  借用原文：A police spokeswoman said that officers were currently in attendance at the scene

questions.prompt: What is Bangalore airport trying to do about the helicopter taxi service?
options: Get approval to add more routes.
Attract more international tourists.
Advertise it through a mobile app.
Make it affordable to common folk.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is Bangalore airport trying to do about the helicopter taxi service? 

 【翻译】 Bangalore机场正试图对直升机出租车服务做些什么? 
 A)  获得批准增加更多航线。 
 B)  吸引更多国际游客。 
 C)  通过移动应用程序进行宣传。 
 D)  使普通民众能负担得起。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Get approval to add more routes. 
 【定位】 P2 The service, which claims to be the first of its kind in India, offers only one route, but Bangalore airport will add more once it gets approval. 
 这项服务号称是印度同类中的首创，目前只提供一条线路，但班加罗尔机场一旦获批就会增加更多线路。 

 【信号】 but 后\+将来动作 。答案句靠两个信号锁定：一是转折词 but，新闻里 but 之后常落真正要说的事；二是将来动作 will add more once it gets approval，正好对应题干"trying to do（正打算做的事）"。 

 【替换】 will add more once it gets approval ↔ Get approval to add more routes 同一动作换序表达 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项 Attract more international tourists. 借"国际"二字勾连录音里的 International Airport terminal（国际机场航站楼），但 International 在原文只是机场名字的一部分，录音从未说机场要"吸引国际游客"，属听到 International 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：International Airport terminal 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Advertise it through a mobile app. 盗用录音 Customers can book their helicopter ride through a mobile app 里的 mobile app，但原文说 app 是用来"预订（book）"的，不是机场用来"打广告（advertise）"，动作被偷换，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：Customers can book their helicopter ride through a mobile app 

 D) 与原文相反 选项 Make it affordable to common folk. 搬来录音里的 affordable，但原文是 Helicopter taxi is not an affordable option for many travelers（对许多人并不便宜），机场也明说 This is not a low cost option，根本没打算降价惠民，选项把"不便宜"反着说成"要让普通人买得起"，是与原文相反的陷阱。  借用原文：Helicopter taxi is not an affordable option for many travelers

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the news report about the helicopter taxi ride?
options: It costs more than twice as much as a car ride.
It is gaining popularity among ordinary Indians.
It symbolizes India's advancement in high-tech.
It can get anywhere in the city within 15 minutes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the news report about the helicopter taxi ride? 

 【翻译】 从新闻报道中我们对直升机出租车服务了解到什么? 
 A)  它的费用是汽车车费的两倍多。 
 B)  它在普通印度人中越来越受欢迎。 
 C)  它象征着印度在高科技领域的进步。 
 D)  它可以在15分钟内到达城市的任何地方。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It costs more than twice as much as a car ride. 
 【定位】 P3 Helicopter taxi is not an affordable option for many travelers. A car ride for the same journey costs less than half as much. 
 直升机出租车对许多旅客来说并不便宜。同样的行程，打车的花费还不到它的一半。 

 【信号】 价格比较句 。答案句是带比较结构的事实陈述 A car ride for the same journey costs less than half as much，含 less than half 这种倍数/比例信号，正对应选项里的价格数字题，是听力里"听到数字/比较就锁定"的典型答案句。 

 【替换】 A car ride for the same journey costs less than half as much ↔ It costs more than twice as much as a car ride 比例反向换算 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 选项 It is gaining popularity among ordinary Indians. 与录音 not an affordable option for many travelers（对许多人并不便宜）相悖——既然普通人嫌贵，就谈不上在"普通印度人"中流行；选项借"印度"这个大背景词制造熟悉感，实则与原文相反。  借用原文：not an affordable option for many travelers 

 C) 过度推断 选项 It symbolizes India’s advancement in high-tech. 把这项服务上升到"象征印度高科技进步"，但录音通篇只讲它的线路、价格、客户、运营方，从未做这种象征性评价，属录音根本没说的过度拔高。 
 D) 原词陷阱 选项 It can get anywhere in the city within 15 minutes. 盗用录音的 15 分钟，但原文 ferry customers the 40 miles between Bangalore’s Electronic City tech hub and the International Airport terminal in 15 minutes 说的是"特定两点间 40 英里 15 分钟"，选项偷偷把范围放大成"城内任何地方"，数字对、范围被改大，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：between Bangalore’s Electronic City tech hub and the International Airport terminal in 15 minutes

questions.prompt: Who are the targeted customers of the helicopter taxi service?
options: International tourists.
High-class travelers.
Prominent superstars.
Customers in a hurry.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Who are the targeted customers of the helicopter taxi service? 

 【翻译】 直升机出租车服务的目标客户是谁? 
 A)  国际游客。 
 B)  高端旅客。 
 C)  知名超级明星。 
 D)  赶时间的顾客。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） High-class travelers. 
 【定位】 P3 "A large number of high-class travelers, including CEOs, have to spend more than three hours by road to get there and that is a loss of time," a Bangalore airport spokesperson said. 
 "包括首席执行官在内的大量高端旅客，开车去那里要花三个多小时，这是时间上的损失，"班加罗尔机场一位发言人说。 

 【信号】 发言人点名人群 。答案句是发言人原话里直接点名的人群 A large number of high-class travelers, including CEOs，新闻里"官方发言人/负责人"的引语常承载关键信息，且这里直接报出目标客户，是最可靠的答案信号。 

 【替换】 A large number of high-class travelers, including CEOs ↔ High-class travelers 原话即选项措辞 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 International tourists. 借 International 勾连录音里多次出现的 International Airport terminal，但原文从没说目标客户是"国际游客"，International 只属于机场名字，属听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：International Airport terminal 

 C) 未提及 选项 Prominent superstars.（知名巨星）在录音里根本没出现，发言人点的是 high-class travelers 和 CEOs，从未提明星；这是"凭直觉觉得贵东西该卖给名人"的常识陷阱，原文无据。 
 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Customers in a hurry. 盗用录音 tech executives in a hurry 里的 in a hurry，但原文 in a hurry 只是修饰"赶时间的科技高管"，回答"为谁服务"的官方表述用的是 high-class travelers 这个上位称呼；选项抓住次要修饰语 in a hurry 当答案，偷换了概念层级，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：tech executives in a hurry

questions.prompt: What does the woman plan to do for the weekend?
options: Treat her friends in a bar.
Take a trip to Washington.
Make some cheese.
Throw a party.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman plan to do for the weekend? 

 【翻译】 女士周末打算做什么? 
 A)  在酒吧请她的朋友们。 
 B)  去华盛顿旅行。 
 C)  做一些奶酪。 
 D)  举办一个聚会。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Throw a party. 
 【定位】 P5 It will be very casual. We will just be a small group of friends gathering together at Washington Park. There will be around 20 of us, including children. 
 会很随意。我们就是一小群朋友聚在华盛顿公园，大约20个人，还带着孩子。 

 【信号】 女方自述聚会安排 。答案藏在女方对自己活动的描述里：a small group of friends gathering together 加上前文 a barbecue this weekend，合起来说明她要办一场朋友聚会/派对，这是问"她计划做什么"时该锁定的自述句。 

 【替换】 a small group of friends gathering together ↔ Throw a party. 聚会即办派对 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文确实有 friends，但聚会在 Washington Park 公园而非酒吧，bar 是凭空加的；选项借"朋友"这个原词诱你选，地点对不上。  借用原文：a small group of friends gathering together at Washington Park 

 B) 原词陷阱 原文 Washington Park 只是聚会地点，选项把 Washington 拎出来说成 take a trip，把"在华盛顿公园聚会"歪曲成"去华盛顿旅行"。  借用原文：gathering together at Washington Park 

 C) 原词陷阱 全程女方是去 buy some cheese，从没说要"做"奶酪；选项借高频词 cheese 诱选，把 buy 偷换成 make。  借用原文：buy some cheese for a barbecue

questions.prompt: What does the man suggest the woman do?
options: Spend no more than 30 dollars.
Buy different kinds of cheese.
Help him prepare the barbecue.
Find out different people's tastes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man suggest the woman do? 

 【翻译】 男士建议女士做什么? 
 A)  花费不超过30美元。 
 B)  购买不同种类的奶酪。 
 C)  帮他准备烧烤。 
 D)  了解不同人的口味。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Buy different kinds of cheese. 
 【定位】 P8 I would suggest having at least one soft cheese and one hard cheese. That will offer you a good variety to suit different people's tastes. 
 我建议至少买一种软奶酪和一种硬奶酪。这样能提供丰富的选择，照顾到不同人的口味。 

 【信号】 建议信号词 suggest 。I would suggest having at least one soft cheese and one hard cheese 里的 suggest 是明确的建议信号，紧随其后的内容就是男方给的建议，正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 one soft cheese and one hard cheese ↔ Buy different kinds of cheese. 软硬各一=多种 
 a good variety to suit different people's tastes ↔ Buy different kinds of cheese. 丰富选择即多种 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 30 dollars 出自女方 Let's say $30.，是她自报的预算，不是男方的建议；选项盗用这个数字，又把它说成"花不超过30"，与"男方建议"无关。  借用原文：Let's say $30. 

 C) 原词陷阱 barbecue 在 a barbecue this weekend 出现过，但男方从未建议女方"帮忙准备烧烤"，help prepare 是凭空添加。  借用原文：a barbecue this weekend 

 D) 原词陷阱 different people's tastes 确在原文 to suit different people's tastes，但它是"买软硬两种"想达到的目的，不是男方让她"去了解口味"这个动作；选项盗用原词却答非所问。  借用原文：to suit different people's tastes

questions.prompt: What does the man say about Spanish goat cheese?
options: It is the best kind of hard cheese.
It is the most popular in Spain.
It is more delicious than honey.
It is a good choice for children.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about Spanish goat cheese? 

 【翻译】 男士对西班牙山羊奶酪有何评价? 
 A)  它是最好的硬质奶酪。 
 B)  它在西班牙最受欢迎。 
 C)  它比蜂蜜更美味。 
 D)  它对儿童来说是个好选择。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is a good choice for children. 
 【定位】 P10 I would suggest something like this Spanish goat cheese. It's only $15, a very good price. You can spread it on bread with a knife, and then add a tiny bit of honey on top. It's delicious. Children love it. 
 我建议这种西班牙山羊奶酪。只要15美元，价格很划算。你可以用刀把它抹在面包上，再在上面加一点蜂蜜，很美味，孩子们都爱吃。 

 【信号】 落点在 Children love it 。讲西班牙山羊奶酪的几句里，结尾 Children love it. 是最贴近选项的评价句，这句直接给出"孩子爱吃"这一可与选项对应的信息。 

 【替换】 Children love it. ↔ It is a good choice for children. 孩子爱吃=适合孩子 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 西班牙山羊奶酪在原文是作为软奶酪 soft cheeses are creamy 举例的，根本不是 hard cheese，更没说"最好的硬奶酪"；best 也是凭空拔高。  借用原文：soft cheeses are creamy and go well with sweet things 

 B) 原词陷阱 Spanish 确实出现在 Spanish goat cheese，但原文只说它产自西班牙/价格好，从没说它"在西班牙最受欢迎"；most popular 是无中生有。  借用原文：this Spanish goat cheese 

 C) 原词陷阱 honey 出自 add a tiny bit of honey on top，原文是说"加点蜂蜜更美味"，并没拿奶酪和蜂蜜比谁更好吃；选项把"配蜂蜜"歪成"比蜂蜜好吃"。  借用原文：add a tiny bit of honey on top. It's delicious.

questions.prompt: What is the woman going to do at the end of the conversation?
options: Buy what the man recommended.
Have a taste of both of the cheeses.
Choose one of the two types of cheese.
Ask the man to cut the cheese into slices.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the woman going to do at the end of the conversation? 

 【翻译】 对话结束时女士打算做什么? 
 A)  购买男士推荐的奶酪。 
 B)  品尝这两种奶酪。 
 C)  在两种奶酪中选择一种。 
 D)  让男士把奶酪切成片。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Buy what the man recommended. 
 【定位】 P13 Okay, I'll take both. Thank you for your help. 
 好的，两种我都要。谢谢你的帮助。 

 【信号】 结尾表态 I'll take both 。对话末句 I'll take both. 是女方的最终拍板，I'll 是结尾决定的信号，这句决定了她要怎么做。 

 【替换】 I'll take both. ↔ Buy what the man recommended. 都要=买他推荐的 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 女方说的是 I'll take both.（两种都买下），不是"先尝两种"；选项盗用"两种"这个概念却把 take（买）偷换成 taste（尝）。  借用原文：I'll take both. 

 C) 与原文相反 原文 I'll take both. 明说"都要"，选项却说"二选一"，方向正好相反；two types 这个原词对得上，结论却反了。  借用原文：I'll take both. 

 D) 张冠李戴 cut...into slices 出自男方介绍硬奶酪 You can cut it into thin slices，是吃法说明，女方结尾从没让对方切片；选项把男方的话安到女方动作上。  借用原文：You can cut it into thin slices and eat it on its own.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about using e-textbooks?
options: New teachers and staff have to be recruited.
It might take some time for students to adapt.
It involves buying lots of tablets and software.
The software has to be constantly upgraded.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about using e-textbooks? 

 【翻译】 女士对使用电子教材有何看法? 
 A)  需要招聘新的教师和工作人员。 
 B)  学生可能需要一些时间来适应。 
 C)  这涉及购买大量平板电脑和软件。 
 D)  软件必须不断升级。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It involves buying lots of tablets and software. 
 【定位】 P2 What about the cost, not only buying all those tablets, but the software and electronic infrastructure that goes with it, not to mention retraining all the teachers and administration staff? 
 那成本怎么办呢？不光是买那些平板，还有随之而来的软件和电子基础设施，更别提还要重新培训所有教师和行政人员了。 

 【信号】 女士用反问抛出顾虑 。男士刚说期待换电子书，女士立刻用 Really? What about the cost 反问抛出"成本"这一顾虑——对话里一方的质疑/反问句往往就是该方观点的答案句，这句把"买平板和软件"列在最前。 

 【替换】 buying all those tablets, but the software ↔ buying lots of tablets and software 原话"买平板和软件"=选项"买大量平板和软件" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音说的是 retraining all the teachers and administration staff（重新培训现有教师和行政人员），A 把它偷换成 New teachers and staff have to be recruited.（招聘新教师和员工）。"培训"不等于"招新人"，听到 staff 一词就选 A 正中陷阱。  借用原文：retraining all the teachers and administration staff 

 B) 未提及 It might take some time for students to adapt. 说学生适应需要时间，但女士的顾虑全在成本和环境上，整段对话没有任何一句谈"学生适应电子书要花时间"，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。 
 D) 张冠李戴 The software has to be constantly upgraded. 的"软件升级"出自男士 the software for electronic readers can be updated instantly，而且男士是把它当"好处"说的；本题问女士的顾虑，把男士的话张冠李戴到女士头上、又把好处当代价，双重错位。  借用原文：the software for electronic readers can be updated instantly

questions.prompt: According to the man, how can the use of tablets benefit students?
options: It can greatly improve their learning efficiency.
It can help them to interact more with teachers.
It can save their trouble of carrying printed books.
It can develop their skills in using electronic devices.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the man, how can the use of tablets benefit students? 

 【翻译】 根据男士的说法,使用平板电脑如何能使学生受益? 
 A)  它可以大大提高他们的学习效率。 
 B)  它可以帮助他们与教师进行更多互动。 
 C)  它可以省去他们携带纸质书籍的麻烦。 
 D)  它可以培养他们使用电子设备的技能。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It can greatly improve their learning efficiency. 
 【定位】 P3 Anyway, tablets help students learn up to 80% faster. 
 总之，平板能帮学生的学习速度提升多达 80%。 

 【信号】 男士用 Anyway 收束抛出核心好处 。男士先回应成本问题，再用 Anyway, tablets help students learn up to 80% faster 把话题收回到"平板的好处"上——Anyway 后的总结句配上 80% 这个具体数字，正是他强调的核心益处，是答案句。 

 【替换】 tablets help students learn up to 80% faster ↔ greatly improve their learning efficiency "学得快 80%"="大幅提升学习效率" 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It can help them to interact more with teachers. 说能多和老师互动，但男士讲的好处是"学得快"和能高亮、记笔记、快速搜索，没有一句提到"与老师互动更多"，是凭"电子设备促进互动"的印象脑补出来的。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音多次出现 printed textbooks/printed books，C 借这个原词编出 It can save their trouble of carrying printed books.（省去背纸质书的麻烦）。但男士说的好处是高亮、记笔记、搜索快，从没说"省得背书"，是听到 printed books 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：printed textbooks 

 D) 偷换概念 录音谈的是 tablets contain many technological features（平板有很多技术功能），D 把它偷换成 It can develop their skills in using electronic devices.（培养学生用电子设备的技能）。男士讲的是功能带来的便利，不是"练会用设备"，借 technological/electronic 这层词制造混淆。  借用原文：tablets contain many technological features

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about students using tablets?
options: They may have trouble comprehending texts.
They may encounter technological problems.
They may pay less respect to teachers.
They may get distracted more easily.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about students using tablets? 

 【翻译】 女士对学生使用平板电脑有何看法? 
 A)  他们可能在理解文本方面遇到困难。 
 B)  他们可能会遇到技术问题。 
 C)  他们可能对教师较少尊重。 
 D)  他们可能更容易分心。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They may get distracted more easily. 
 【定位】 P4 Not necessarily. Tablets have too many distractions. Students may pay attention to apps, games and websites instead of their teachers. 
 未必。平板有太多让人分心的东西。学生可能会去关注各种应用、游戏和网站，而不是听老师讲课。 

 【信号】 Not necessarily 否定后才是女士真意 。女士用 Not necessarily 先否定男士"学得快"的说法，紧接着抛出 Tablets have too many distractions——否定/转折之后亮出的才是她真正要说的弊端，distractions 这个词直接对应"分心"。 

 【替换】 Tablets have too many distractions ↔ get distracted more easily "有太多让人分心的东西"="更容易分心" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音说 people who read printed text comprehend more（读纸质的人理解得更多），A 借 comprehend 这个词编成 They may have trouble comprehending texts.（理解文字有困难）。原文是"读纸质理解更多"的对比，不是说学生用平板"看不懂"，听到 comprehend 就选即落陷阱。  借用原文：people who read printed text comprehend more 

 B) 未提及 They may encounter technological problems. 说学生会遇到技术问题，但女士谈的是分心和纸质阅读理解更好，全程没说"学生用平板会碰到技术故障"，是凭"用电子设备会出故障"的常识补出来的。 
 C) 偷换概念 录音说学生可能 pay attention to apps, games and websites instead of their teachers（去看应用游戏而非听老师），C 借 teachers 偷换成 They may pay less respect to teachers.（不那么尊重老师）。原文说的是"注意力不在老师身上"，不是"不尊重老师"，听到 teachers 就选即中招。  借用原文：pay attention to apps, games and websites instead of their teachers

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about making electronic readers?
options: It generates a great deal of electronic garbage.
It does a lot of damage to the environment.
It emits huge amounts of harmful radiation.
It accelerates the exhaustion of rare minerals.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about making electronic readers? 

 【翻译】 女士对制造电子阅读器有何看法? 
 A)  它产生大量电子垃圾。 
 B)  它对环境造成很大破坏。 
 C)  它排放大量有害辐射。 
 D)  它加速稀有矿物的枯竭。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It does a lot of damage to the environment. 
 【定位】 P6 Actually, manufacturing tablets is environmentally destructive and dangerous to human health. A lot of minerals are extracted from the earth to make electronic readers. It does far more damage to the environment. 
 实际上，制造平板对环境有破坏性，也危害人体健康。要从地里开采大量矿物来制造电子阅读器。它对环境造成的破坏要大得多。 

 【信号】 末句 It does far more damage 是收束结论 。女士这段先说制造平板 environmentally destructive，列举健康危害和开采矿物，最后用 It does far more damage to the environment 一句收束——段末的总括性结论句正是她对"制造电子阅读器"的核心表态，是答案句。 

 【替换】 It does far more damage to the environment ↔ does a lot of damage to the environment "破坏环境大得多"="对环境造成很大破坏" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It generates a great deal of electronic garbage. 说产生大量电子垃圾，但女士谈的是健康危害、开采矿物、破坏环境，没有一句提到"电子垃圾/garbage"，是把环保话题往"电子垃圾"这个常见印象上靠的未提及项。 
 C) 未提及 It emits huge amounts of harmful radiation. 说释放大量有害辐射，听上去很吓人，但女士只说 destructive、dangerous to health、extract minerals，从没说"辐射/radiation"，是凭"电子产品有辐射"的印象编的未提及项。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 A lot of minerals are extracted from the earth to make electronic readers（开采大量矿物来造电子阅读器），D 借 minerals 编成 It accelerates the exhaustion of rare minerals.（加速稀有矿物枯竭）。原文说的是"开采矿物"这一事实，没说"加速枯竭"这个后果，且本题要的是女士的总括结论（破坏环境），D 是中途细节的过度引申。  借用原文：A lot of minerals are extracted from the earth to make electronic readers

questions.prompt: What does the passage say we tend to do every day?
options: Communicate with our coworkers.
Encounter people in different places.
Judge people based on our first impressions.
Engage in a variety of psychological activities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say we tend to do every day? 

 【翻译】 文章说我们每天倾向于做什么？ 
 A)  与同事交流。 
 B)  在不同地方遇见人。 
 C)  根据第一印象判断他人。 
 D)  从事各种心理活动。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Judge people based on our first impressions. 
 【定位】 P1 Consider how often you make this kind of judgment every day. When you meet with a new coworker, you immediately begin to develop an initial impression of this person. 
 想想你每天多频繁地做出这种评判。当你见到一位新同事，你立刻就开始形成对这个人的最初印象。 

 【信号】 every day 原词复现+举例佐证 。录音用 Consider how often you make this kind of judgment every day 直接点出我们每天都在做的这件事就是 judgment（评判），随后用见新同事就 develop an initial impression 的例子佐证，every day 与题干同词，是答案句的定位信号。 

 【替换】 this kind of judgment ↔ Judge people based on our first impressions judgment 名词→Judge 动词同根 
 develop an initial impression ↔ based on our first impressions initial impression=first impression 同义 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实出现 When you meet with a new coworker，A 项 Communicate with our coworkers. 借了 coworker 这个原词，但录音说的是见到新同事时会形成印象，不是与同事沟通，盗词却答非所问。  借用原文：When you meet with a new coworker 

 B) 偷换概念 录音有 When you visit the grocery store 这个去不同地方的例子，B 项 Encounter people in different places. 借此包装成在不同地方遇见人，但录音此处讲的仍是对收银员形成评判，不是强调遇见人这件事本身，属把例子细节偷换成选项主语。  借用原文：When you visit the grocery store 

 D) 过度推断 录音讲的是一种具体行为——做评判、形成印象，D 项 Engage in a variety of psychological activities. 用 a variety of psychological activities 把它说得又大又泛，范围被夸大，不是录音点名的那一件每天做的事。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about person perception from this passage?
options: It is an objective evaluation of a person's character.
It is a mental process influenced by many factors.
It contributes to the formation of personal traits.
It varies greatly among different social groups.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about person perception from this passage? 

 【翻译】 从这篇文章中我们对人际知觉了解到什么？ 
 A)  它是对一个人性格的客观评价。 
 B)  它是一个受许多因素影响的心理过程。 
 C)  它有助于个人特质的形成。 
 D)  它在不同社会群体中差异很大。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It is a mental process influenced by many factors. 
 【定位】 P2 Obviously, person perception is a very subjective process that can be affected by a number of variables, including the characteristics of the person you are observing, the context of the situation, your own personal traits, and your past experiences. 
 显然，识人知觉是一个非常主观的过程，会受到许多变量的影响，包括你所观察对象的特征、情境的背景、你自身的性格特质，以及你过往的经历。 

 【信号】 Obviously 强调+定性句 。录音用 Obviously 加重语气引出对该概念的定性，紧接着 a very subjective process that can be affected by a number of variables 直接说它是主观的、受许多变量影响，这是专门给 person perception 定性的答案句。 

 【替换】 a very subjective process ↔ It is a mental process influenced by many factors subjective process=mental process 
 affected by a number of variables ↔ influenced by many factors affected by variables=influenced by factors 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音明说它是 a very subjective process（主观过程），A 项 It is an objective evaluation of a person's character. 却说成 objective（客观），把性质说反了，且 evaluation、character 也只是蹭话题词。  借用原文：a very subjective process 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 your own personal traits 是影响 person perception 的因素之一，C 项 It contributes to the formation of personal traits. 却反过来说它造就了性格特质，借了 personal traits 这个原词，但把因果方向整个调反了。  借用原文：your own personal traits 

 D) 未提及 D 项 It varies greatly among different social groups. 说它在不同社会群体间差异巨大，但录音讲的是它受个人层面的多种变量影响，从未提到社会群体之间的差异，属凭空添加。

questions.prompt: What is the problem with using social categorization in person perception?
options: It can lead to incorrect judgments.
It can cause mistrust among people.
It can result in instant losses.
It can give rise to gender bias.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the problem with using social categorization in person perception? 

 【翻译】 在人际知觉中使用社会分类有什么问题？ 
 A)  它可能导致错误的判断。 
 B)  它可能引起人与人之间的不信任。 
 C)  它可能造成即时损失。 
 D)  它可能引发性别偏见。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It can lead to incorrect judgments. 
 【定位】 P4 Problems with this technique include the fact that it can lead to errors and prejudice. 
 这种方法的问题包括：它会导致错误和偏见。 

 【信号】 Problems 原词+lead to errors 。录音用 Problems with this technique 直接对应题干的 problem，紧跟 it can lead to errors and prejudice 点出弊端就是导致错误和偏见，Problems 一词与题干同义，是定位答案句的强信号。 

 【替换】 it can lead to errors ↔ It can lead to incorrect judgments errors=incorrect judgments 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 B 项 It can cause mistrust among people. 说会造成人际不信任，但录音讲的弊端是 errors and prejudice（错误与偏见），从没说到不信任，属凭空添加的后果。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音例子结尾说被偷了钱包 leading to the loss of your wallet，C 项 It can result in instant losses. 借 loss 这个原词包装成即时损失，但那只是一个具体例子的细节，本题问的是 social categorization 的整体弊端（错误与偏见），盗词答非所问，且 instant 也是录音没有的。  借用原文：leading to the loss of your wallet 

 D) 偷换概念 录音说弊端含 prejudice（偏见），D 项 It can give rise to gender bias. 借偏见这层意思却收窄成性别偏见，录音例子讲的是凭老妇与壮汉的外貌分类，从没限定为性别偏见，属以偏概全。  借用原文：prejudice

questions.prompt: What does the new study suggest about young people today and those from the previous generation?
options: Both groups spend a lot of time on mobile devices.
Both groups attach importance to social connections.
They are equally competent in using new technology.
They are similar in terms of social skills.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the new study suggest about young people today and those from the previous generation? 

 【翻译】 新研究对当今年轻人和上一代人有何提示? 
 A)  两个群体都在移动设备上花费大量时间。 
 B)  两个群体都重视社会联系。 
 C)  他们在使用新技术方面同样有能力。 
 D)  他们在社交技能方面相似。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They are similar in terms of social skills. 
 【定位】 P1 Despite smartphones and social media, young people today are as socially competent as those from the previous generation. 
 尽管有智能手机和社交媒体，今天的年轻人在社交能力上与上一代人不相上下。 

 【信号】 让步 Despite 后才是真意 。答案信号是让步词 Despite smartphones and social media——让步状语先抛出一个看似负面的前提，真正的研究结论在它之后的主句 young people today are as socially competent as those from the previous generation，这种 Despite／Although 后的主句正是篇章听力的高频落点。 

 【替换】 as socially competent as those from the previous generation ↔ They are similar in terms of social skills. as…as 等同改写成 similar 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音开头确实念到 smartphones and social media，A 项 Both groups spend a lot of time on mobile devices. 借这个原词诱你选，但原文只说尽管有手机、社交能力照样相当，从没说两代人都花大量时间在设备上，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：smartphones and social media 

 B) 未提及 B 项 Both groups attach importance to social connections. 说两代都重视社交联系，但原文只比较社交能力强弱（competent），从未说他们重视或看重社交，研究里没有这层意思。 
 C) 偷换概念 录音提到 mobile devices were widespread，C 项 They are equally competent in using new technology. 借 technology 与 competent 两个耳熟词诱选，但原文说的是社交能力（socially competent）相当，不是使用技术的能力相当，把社交能力偷换成了用技术的能力。  借用原文：mobile devices were widespread

questions.prompt: What did the study find about children who accessed social networking sites many times a day?
options: Their social skills were negatively affected.
Their school performance was slightly lower.
Their emotions were much harder to regulate.
Their relations with peers were badly strained.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the study find about children who accessed social networking sites many times a day? 

 【翻译】 该研究对每天多次访问社交网站的儿童有何发现? 
 A)  他们的社交技能受到了负面影响。 
 B)  他们的学业表现略有下降。 
 C)  他们的情绪更加难以调节。 
 D)  他们与同龄人的关系严重紧张。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Their social skills were negatively affected. 
 【定位】 P4 There was one exception: Social skills were slightly lower for children who accessed online games and social networking sites many times a day. 
 有一个例外：对于每天多次玩网络游戏和上社交网站的孩子，他们的社交能力略低一些。 

 【信号】 例外 one exception 即落点 。答案信号是转折式提示词 There was one exception——前文一直说社交能力保持不变或提升，唯独这个 exception 后面交代了负面发现 Social skills were slightly lower，例外句是典型的答案落点。 

 【替换】 Social skills were slightly lower ↔ Their social skills were negatively affected. 变低概括为受负面影响 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音里 slightly lower 修饰的是 social skills（社交能力），B 项 Their school performance was slightly lower. 原封不动搬来 slightly lower，却把对象换成学业表现，原文从没说成绩略低，属听到 slightly lower 就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：Social skills were slightly lower 

 C) 张冠李戴 录音在第 3 段提过 regulate their temper，C 项 Their emotions were much harder to regulate. 借 regulate 诱选，但那是第 3 段讲两组孩子在自控上相似时的话，跟第 4 段每天多次上网那群孩子无关，且程度被夸成 much harder，与原文 slightly 相反。  借用原文：regulate their temper 

 D) 过度推断 D 项 Their relations with peers were badly strained. 说同伴关系严重紧张，原文既没说这群孩子的同伴关系受损，也没用 badly 这种重程度词（原文是 slightly），属夸大加无中生有。

questions.prompt: What is adults' worry about technological change?
options: It may pose a threat to their children's safety.
It may affect society's traditional values.
It may hurt their relations with children.
It may change their children's ethical values.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is adults' worry about technological change? 

 【翻译】 成年人对技术变革的担忧是什么? 
 A)  它可能对他们孩子的安全构成威胁。 
 B)  它可能影响社会的传统价值观。 
 C)  它可能损害他们与孩子的关系。 
 D)  它可能改变他们孩子的伦理价值观。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It may hurt their relations with children. 
 【定位】 P5 Adults are worried when technological change starts to undermine traditional relationships, particularly the parent-child relationship. 
 当科技变化开始侵蚀传统关系、尤其是亲子关系时，成年人会感到担忧。 

 【信号】 worried 直陈担忧 + particularly 点重点 。答案信号是表担忧的谓语 Adults are worried，其担忧对象由 undermine traditional relationships 给出，再由强调词 particularly the parent-child relationship 把重点收窄到亲子关系——particularly 后面的限定正是答案要的具体落点。 

 【替换】 undermine traditional relationships, particularly the parent-child relationship ↔ It may hurt their relations with children. undermine=hurt，parent-child=with children 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 It may pose a threat to their children's safety. 借耳熟的 children 诱选，但原文成年人担忧的是亲子关系被侵蚀，从没提孩子的人身安全（safety），属新增内容。 
 B) 偷换概念 录音念过 traditional relationships 与第 6 段的 moral panic，B 项 It may affect society's traditional values. 借 traditional 诱选，但原文担忧的是传统关系（relationships），不是社会传统价值（values），把关系偷换成了价值观。  借用原文：traditional relationships 

 D) 过度推断 第 6 段提到 moral panic，D 项 It may change their children's ethical values. 借这条道德暗线诱选，但 moral panic 指成年人面对新技术的恐慌情绪，原文从未说科技会改变孩子的道德／伦理价值观，属由 moral 一词过度推断。  借用原文：moral panic

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about inspiration from consuming others' ideas and success stories?
options: It is motivating.
It is passive.
It is incredible.
It is impracticable.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about inspiration from consuming others' ideas and success stories? 

 【翻译】 说话人对于从他人的想法和成功故事中获取灵感有何看法? 
 A)  它具有激励作用。 
 B)  它是被动的。 
 C)  它令人难以置信。 
 D)  它不切实际。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It is passive. 
 【定位】 P2 The problem is that consuming the success and ideas of others is passive inspiration. 
 问题在于，消费他人的成功与想法，是一种被动的灵感。 

 【信号】 下定义句 is + 定性词 。这句用 consuming the success and ideas of others is passive inspiration 的 "A is B" 结构，直接给 "消费他人成功" 贴上 passive inspiration 的标签，是典型的下定义信号，定性题答案就藏在这种 "...is..." 的判断里。 

 【替换】 passive inspiration ↔ It is passive. 原词原义直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音把 consuming 来的灵感判为 passive（被动），而 It is motivating. 说它有激励性，恰与原文相反，是把被动说成主动激励。  借用原文：passive inspiration 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音 P1 确实出现过 incredible videos, articles and news stories，incredible 是用来形容那些视频文章 "很精彩"，并不是给 passive inspiration 的定性；选项 It is incredible. 盗这个原词来骗 "听到就选"。  借用原文：incredible videos, articles and news stories 

 D) 未提及 录音从未说 consuming 来的 inspiration 是 impracticable（不切实际的），原文只说它 passive、不能代替自己创造，并没有 "不可行" 这层意思，属凭空添加。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about active inspiration?
options: It results in short-term excitement.
It helps us avoid making mistakes.
It breeds long-term passion and enthusiasm.
It is bound to help us achieve greater success.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the passage about active inspiration? 

 【翻译】 从文章中我们对主动灵感了解到什么? 
 A)  它会产生短期的兴奋感。 
 B)  它帮助我们避免犯错。 
 C)  它孕育长期的热情和热忱。 
 D)  它必定会帮助我们取得更大的成功。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It breeds long-term passion and enthusiasm. 
 【定位】 P3 Furthermore, active inspiration is what results in long-term passion and enthusiasm. 
 此外，主动的灵感正是带来长久热情与激情的东西。 

 【信号】 递进 Furthermore 后给定论 。Furthermore, active inspiration is what results in long-term passion and enthusiasm 由 Furthermore 引出对 active inspiration 的进一步定论，递进词后常接观点落点；同时 results in 是因果信号，直接给出它的结果。 

 【替换】 results in long-term passion and enthusiasm ↔ It breeds long-term passion and enthusiasm. results in 同义替换为 breeds 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 录音说 short-term 的是 watching 别人成功带来的兴奋——Watching someone else's success might leave you feeling excited for a few minutes，那是 passive 一侧的效果；It results in short-term excitement. 把这份 "短暂兴奋" 安到 active inspiration 头上，张冠李戴。  借用原文：Watching someone else's success might leave you feeling excited for a few minutes 

 B) 与原文相反 录音讲 active inspiration 包含 making mistakes（犯错）才认识自我，从没说它能 avoid making mistakes（避免犯错），It helps us avoid making mistakes. 把原文里的 "犯错" 反着安成 "避免犯错"，原文无此说法。  借用原文：making mistakes that we discover who we are 

 D) 过度推断 录音只说 active inspiration 带来长期热情、给你 power，并没有保证它 "必然带来更大成功"；It is bound to help us achieve greater success. 中 bound to（必定）把效果夸成必然成功，推过了头。  借用原文：active inspiration is what results in long-term passion and enthusiasm

questions.prompt: What does the passage say passive inspiration can do?
options: Drive us forward.
Bring us power.
Spur us to action.
Give us ideas.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say passive inspiration can do? 

 【翻译】 文章指出被动灵感能做什么? 
 A)  推动我们前进。 
 B)  给我们带来力量。 
 C)  激励我们采取行动。 
 D)  给我们提供想法。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Give us ideas. 
 【定位】 P4 Passive inspiration can give you ideas, but active inspiration will give you power. 
 被动的灵感能给你想法，但主动的灵感会给你力量。 

 【信号】 对比句 but 两侧分派功能 。Passive inspiration can give you ideas, but active inspiration will give you power 用 but 把两种 inspiration 的功能并排对照，passive 给 ideas、active 给 power；对比句两侧的分工正是答案点，须按主语取属于 passive 的那半句。 

 【替换】 Passive inspiration can give you ideas ↔ Give us ideas. give you ideas 改 give us ideas 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 录音 P4 说 creating, producing, and experimenting is what drives you forward，drive forward 是 active 一侧（创造、试验）的功能；Drive us forward. 把它安到 passive 头上，张冠李戴。  借用原文：creating, producing, and experimenting is what drives you forward 

 B) 原词陷阱 对比句明说 active inspiration will give you power，给 power 的是 active；Bring us power. 盗用原词 power 却把它派给 passive，正中 but 后半句被对调的陷阱。  借用原文：active inspiration will give you power 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音 P3 出现过 taking action and applying a new idea to your life，action 是讲 active inspiration 的语境，且原文并无 "passive 能 spur us to action" 的说法；Spur us to action. 借 action 这个原词制造熟悉感，却答非所问。  借用原文：taking action and applying a new idea to your life

questions.prompt: Where does the best inspiration come from according to the passage?
options: Listening to success stories.
Applying ideas to one's life.
Following the advice of experts.
Consuming the world around us.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where does the best inspiration come from according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章,最好的灵感来自哪里? 
 A)  倾听成功故事。 
 B)  将想法应用到自己的生活中。 
 C)  遵循专家的建议。 
 D)  接纳我们周围的世界。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Applying ideas to one's life. 
 【定位】 P5 The best inspiration comes from the application of ideas, not the consumption of them. 
 最好的灵感来自对想法的应用，而非对它们的消费。 

 【信号】 结尾总括句 the best...comes from 。The best inspiration comes from the application of ideas, not the consumption of them 是末段收束的总括定调句，the best...comes from 直接给出结论，且用 not 把对立的 consumption 排掉，是篇章结尾的答案落点信号。 

 【替换】 the application of ideas ↔ Applying ideas to one's life. 名词 application 还原为动词 applying 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音讲的是 application 对 consumption，并没说最佳灵感来自 "listening to success stories（听成功故事）"，反倒把 "听别人成功" 归为 passive；Listening to success stories. 与结论相悖。  借用原文：Hearing about other people's success isn't the same as creating your own 

 C) 未提及 全文从未提到 "following the advice of experts（听从专家建议）"，没有任何对应句，属凭空添加的来源。 
 D) 与原文相反 结尾 not the consumption of them 明确用 not 把 consumption 排在最佳来源之外，Consuming the world around us. 盗用录音确实念过的 consuming/consumption，却恰恰选了被否定的那一极。  借用原文：not the consumption of them
